title: The shared emergency-contact bridge

known_project_facts.project: A disaster-relief intake service wants to deduplicate adult beneficiaries across mobile outreach and shelter registrations. Linking changes eligibility decisions; this is a design exercise, not deployment authorization.
known_project_facts.identity: Same natural person, not household, caregiver, or emergency contact.
known_project_facts.current_pipeline: Name + birth-year and phone blocks; hand-weighted pair scores; above-threshold links are closed transitively into one beneficiary.

observations.evidence: same contact phone; similar abbreviated name
same contact phone; same temporary shelter
different verified adult birth dates; distinct intake photographs reviewed by staff

known_project_facts.data_notes: The phone belongs to a volunteer helping multiple adults; a verified birth date may still have transcription errors. Scores are uncalibrated, not probabilities.
known_project_facts.constraints: A false merge can suppress aid to an individual. Staff can review 40 ambiguous groups daily. Membership must be reversible. No ground-truth entity partition is yet available.

explicitly_unknown: How independently reliable are birth-date contradictions?
How many beneficiary groups are affected and how representative are reviewed cases?
What evidence and authorization permit irreversible identity decisions?
task: Produce a defensible project-specific ER experiment/design recommendation using selectively retrieved Atlas knowledge if available. Do not implement ER or change production. Separate facts, assumptions, uncertainties, mechanisms and proposed evidence.
